ko.title: [소비자 심리학 #6] 웃긴 광고가 과자는 팔아도 자동차는 못 파는 이유: 설득은 실제로 어떻게 작동하는가

segments.src: > An ad persuades in different ways depending on how much you care and how closely you're paying attention. Fear and humor can both work, but only when they're used carefully.
segments.tr: > 광고는 소비자가 얼마나 신경 쓰고 얼마나 주의를 기울이는지에 따라 서로 다른 방식으로 설득합니다. 공포와 유머 모두 효과가 있을 수 있지만, 신중하게 사용될 때만 그렇습니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Every ad is trying to change something in your head, whether that's a belief ("this brand is reliable"), a feeling ("this brand is fun"), or a behavior ("buy now").
segments.tr: 모든 광고는 여러분의 머릿속 무언가를 바꾸려 합니다. 그것이 신념(“이 브랜드는 믿을 만하다”), 감정(“이 브랜드는 재미있다”), 행동(“지금 구매하세요”)이든 말이죠.

segments.src: Persuasion is the process of making that change.
segments.tr: 설득은 그 변화를 만들어내는 과정입니다.

segments.src: Researchers have spent decades studying **why some messages work and others don't.**
segments.tr: 연구자들은 수십 년 동안 **왜 어떤 메시지는 효과가 있고 어떤 메시지는 없는지**를 연구해 왔습니다.

segments.src: The Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM)**
segments.tr: 정교화 가능성 모델(ELM)**

segments.src: Psychologists Richard Petty and John Cacioppo proposed the ELM in the 1980s.
segments.tr: 심리학자 리처드 페티(Richard Petty)와 존 카시오포(John Cacioppo)는 1980년대에 ELM을 제안했습니다.

segments.src: Its main idea is that people process a persuasive message along one of two routes:
segments.tr: 이 모델의 핵심 아이디어는 사람들이 설득 메시지를 두 가지 경로 중 하나를 따라 처리한다는 것입니다:

segments.src: - **Central route.** You think carefully about the message: Is the evidence good? Do the claims hold up? People take this route when they are **motivated** (the decision matters to them) and **able** (they have the time, attention, and knowledge). Attitudes formed this way tend to last longer and are harder to change.
segments.tr: - **중심 경로.** 여러분은 메시지를 신중하게 생각합니다. 근거가 좋은가? 주장이 타당한가? 사람들은 **동기**(결정이 자신에게 중요함)와 **능력**(시간, 주의력, 지식이 있음)이 있을 때 이 경로를 택합니다. 이런 방식으로 형성된 태도는 더 오래 지속되고 바꾸기도 더 어렵습니다.

segments.src: - **Peripheral route.** You rely on shortcuts such as an attractive spokesperson, a catchy jingle, a celebrity, or simply "lots of people bought it." People take this route when they're distracted, in a hurry, or don't care much. Attitudes formed this way can shift quickly, and they can fade just as quickly.
segments.tr: - **주변 경로.** 여러분은 매력적인 모델, 귀에 맴도는 징글, 유명인, 또는 단순히 “많은 사람이 샀다”는 사실 같은 지름길에 의존합니다. 사람들은 산만하거나, 서두르거나, 별로 신경 쓰지 않을 때 이 경로를 택합니다. 이런 방식으로 형성된 태도는 빠르게 바뀔 수 있으며, 그만큼 빠르게 사라지기도 합니다.

segments.src: "Elaboration" just means how much you think about the message.
segments.tr: ‘정교화’는 메시지를 얼마나 깊이 생각하는지를 뜻합니다.

segments.src: The same ad can persuade one person through careful reasoning and another through a smiling face.
segments.tr: 같은 광고라도 어떤 사람은 신중한 추론을 통해, 다른 사람은 미소 짓는 얼굴을 보고 설득될 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Fear appeals**
segments.tr: 공포 소구**

segments.src: A fear appeal shows a threat, such as illness, an accident, or financial loss, to motivate action.
segments.tr: 공포 소구는 질병, 사고, 재정적 손실 같은 위협을 보여주어 행동을 유도합니다.

segments.src: Research, including Kim Witte's Extended Parallel Process Model, suggests that fear works only when it comes with **efficacy**: the audience has to believe there's a clear, doable step that will actually protect them.
segments.tr: Kim Witte의 확장 병렬 과정 모델(Extended Parallel Process Model)을 포함한 연구들은, 공포가 **효능감**과 함께 제시될 때만 효과가 있다고 봅니다. 즉, 수용자가 자신을 실제로 보호할 수 있는 명확하고 실행 가능한 단계가 있다고 믿어야 한다는 것입니다.

segments.src: When a message has high threat and low efficacy, people often push it away instead of acting on it.
segments.tr: 위협은 높고 효능감은 낮은 메시지는, 사람들이 행동하기보다 거부하는 경우가 많습니다.

segments.src: They avoid the topic, doubt the source, or tell themselves "it won't happen to me."
segments.tr: 그들은 주제를 피하거나, 출처를 의심하거나, “나에게는 일어나지 않을 일이야”라고 스스로를 달랩니다.

segments.src: Scaring people harder doesn't automatically make the message work better.
segments.tr: 사람들을 더 세게 겁준다고 해서 메시지가 자동으로 더 잘 먹히는 것은 아닙니다.

segments.src: Humor appeals**
segments.tr: 유머 소구**

segments.src: Humor grabs attention and makes people like the ad, and that good feeling can rub off on the brand.
segments.tr: 유머는 주의를 끌고 사람들이 광고를 좋아하게 만들며, 그 좋은 느낌이 브랜드에도 옮겨 갈 수 있습니다.

segments.src: It has downsides, though:
segments.tr: 하지만 단점도 있습니다:

segments.src: - It can **distract** viewers from the actual product information.
segments.tr: - 실제 제품 정보로부터 시청자의 **주의를 흩뜨릴** 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - People may remember the joke and forget the brand, which practitioners sometimes call the "vampire effect."
segments.tr: - 사람들이 농담은 기억하면서 브랜드는 잊을 수 있는데, 업계에서는 이를 “뱀파이어 효과”라고 부르기도 합니다.

segments.src: - It usually works better for **familiar, low-risk, low-involvement products** (snacks, soda, fast food) than for complex or high-stakes purchases.
segments.tr: - 보통 복잡하거나 고위험인 구매보다 **익숙하고, 위험이 낮으며, 관여도가 낮은 제품**(간식, 탄산음료, 패스트푸드)에서 더 잘 작동합니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: Jordan, who lives in Columbus, Ohio, is watching football on Sunday.
segments.tr: 오하이오주 콜럼버스에 사는 Jordan은 일요일에 미식축구를 보고 있습니다.

segments.src: During a commercial break, a goofy car insurance ad gets a laugh.
segments.tr: 광고 시간에 우스꽝스러운 자동차 보험 광고가 나와 웃음을 줍니다.

segments.src: Jordan isn't shopping for insurance right now, so the joke and the memorable mascot are basically all that sticks.
segments.tr: Jordan은 지금 보험을 알아보는 중이 아니므로, 기억에 남는 것은 농담과 인상적인 마스코트뿐입니다.

segments.src: That's the **peripheral route**, and it worked: the brand name is now in Jordan's head.
segments.tr: 이것이 **주변 경로**이고, 효과도 있었습니다. 이제 브랜드 이름이 Jordan의 머릿속에 들어갔으니까요.

segments.src: Three weeks later, Jordan's policy is up for renewal, and the quotes are around $1,400 a year.
segments.tr: 3주 후, Jordan의 보험 계약이 갱신 시기가 되었고 견적은 연간 약 $1,400입니다.

segments.src: Now Jordan is motivated and sits down with a laptop to compare deductibles, liability limits, and customer reviews.
segments.tr: 이제 Jordan은 동기가 생겨 노트북 앞에 앉아 자기부담금, 배상 책임 한도, 고객 리뷰를 비교합니다.

segments.src: That's the **central route**.
segments.tr: 이것이 **중심 경로**입니다.

segments.src: A funny ad won't close this sale.
segments.tr: 웃긴 광고로는 이 판매를 성사시킬 수 없습니다.

segments.src: Clear numbers and believable claims will.
segments.tr: 명확한 수치와 믿을 만한 주장이 그것을 해냅니다.

segments.src: Later that week, Jordan sees a public service ad from the CDC's long-running "Tips From Former Smokers" campaign, which features real people living with smoking-related illnesses.
segments.tr: 같은 주 후반에 Jordan은 CDC의 장기 캠페인 “Tips From Former Smokers”의 공익 광고를 봅니다. 이 광고는 흡연과 관련된 질병을 안고 사는 실제 사람들을 등장시킵니다.

segments.src: The ad is frightening, but it ends with a concrete step: call 1-800-QUIT-NOW for free help.
segments.tr: 광고는 무섭지만, 구체적인 행동 요령으로 끝납니다. 무료 도움을 받으려면 1-800-QUIT-NOW로 전화하라는 것입니다.

segments.src: It pairs **threat with efficacy**, which is how a fear appeal is supposed to be built.
segments.tr: 이 광고는 **위협과 효능감을 짝지어** 보여주는데, 이것이 바로 공포 소구가 만들어져야 하는 방식입니다.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: 1. According to the ELM, people process ads through a careful **central route** or a shortcut-based **peripheral route**, depending on their motivation and ability.
segments.tr: 1. ELM에 따르면, 사람들은 동기와 능력에 따라 광고를 신중한 **중심 경로** 또는 지름길에 의존하는 **주변 경로**로 처리합니다.

segments.src: 2. **Fear appeals** work best when the threat comes with a clear, doable solution. Fear without a way out tends to cause avoidance.
segments.tr: 2. **공포 소구**는 위협과 함께 명확하고 실행 가능한 해결책이 제시될 때 가장 효과적입니다. 빠져나갈 길 없는 공포는 회피를 낳는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: 3. **Humor** boosts attention and liking but can bury the message. It fits low-involvement products better than high-stakes ones.
segments.tr: 3. **유머**는 주의와 호감을 높이지만 메시지를 묻어버릴 수 있습니다. 고관여 제품보다 저관여 제품에 더 잘 맞습니다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 자가 퀴즈

segments.src: **Q1.** According to the ELM, which situation makes the central route most likely?
segments.tr: **Q1.** ELM에 따르면, 어떤 상황에서 중심 경로가 가장 가능성이 높을까요?

segments.src: - A) Scrolling past an ad while chatting with friends
segments.tr: - A) 친구와 대화하면서 광고를 스크롤로 넘길 때

segments.src: - B) Researching a new $30,000 car you plan to buy next month
segments.tr: - B) 다음 달 구매할 예정인 3만 달러짜리 새 차를 조사할 때

segments.src: - C) Hearing a jingle on the radio while driving
segments.tr: - C) 운전 중 라디오에서 징글을 들을 때

segments.src: - D) Seeing a celebrity holding a soda can
segments.tr: - D) 유명인이 음료수 캔을 들고 있는 것을 볼 때

segments.src: **Q2.** (True/False) The scarier a fear appeal is, the more effective it always becomes.
segments.tr: **Q2.** (참/거짓) 공포 소구가 무서울수록 항상 더 효과적이 된다.

segments.src: **Q3.** Which is a known risk of humor appeals?
segments.tr: **Q3.** 유머 소구의 알려진 위험은 무엇인가?

segments.src: - A) Viewers remember the joke but forget the brand
segments.tr: - A) 시청자가 농담은 기억하지만 브랜드는 잊는다

segments.src: - B) Humor always lowers attention
segments.tr: - B) 유머는 항상 주의를 떨어뜨린다

segments.src: - C) Humor only works for expensive products
segments.tr: - C) 유머는 비싼 제품에만 효과가 있다

segments.src: - D) Humor makes ads illegal in some states
segments.tr: - D) 유머는 일부 주에서 광고를 불법으로 만든다

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM):** A theory stating that persuasion happens through either careful thinking (central route) or mental shortcuts (peripheral route).
segments.tr: - **정교화 가능성 모델(ELM):** 설득이 신중한 사고(중심 경로) 또는 정신적 지름길(주변 경로)을 통해 일어난다고 설명하는 이론.

segments.src: - **Central route:** Being persuaded by carefully evaluating the arguments and evidence in a message.
segments.tr: - **중심 경로:** 메시지에 담긴 주장과 근거를 신중하게 평가하여 설득되는 것.

segments.src: - **Peripheral route:** Being persuaded by surface cues such as attractiveness, celebrity, music, or popularity.
segments.tr: - **주변 경로:** 매력, 유명인, 음악, 인기 같은 표면적 단서에 의해 설득되는 것.

segments.src: - **Fear appeal:** A message that highlights a threat to motivate protective action. It works best when paired with a clear solution (efficacy).
segments.tr: - **공포 소구:** 보호 행동을 유도하기 위해 위협을 강조하는 메시지. 명확한 해결책(효능감)과 짝지어질 때 가장 효과적이다.

segments.src: - **Humor appeal:** Using comedy in a message to capture attention and build positive feelings toward a brand.
segments.tr: - **유머 소구:** 주의를 끌고 브랜드에 대한 긍정적 감정을 쌓기 위해 메시지에 코미디를 사용하는 것.

segments.src: *Answers: Q1 – B.
segments.tr: *정답: Q1 – B.

segments.src: A big, personally important purchase gives you both the motivation and the time to weigh the details, which is the central route.
segments.tr: 크고 개인적으로 중요한 구매는 동기와 세부 사항을 따져볼 시간을 함께 주므로, 중심 경로에 해당합니다.

segments.src: Q2 – False.
segments.tr: Q2 – 거짓.

segments.src: Without a believable, doable solution, very strong fear often leads people to avoid or reject the message.
segments.tr: 믿을 만하고 실행 가능한 해결책이 없으면, 아주 강한 공포는 사람들이 메시지를 회피하거나 거부하게 만드는 경우가 많습니다.

segments.src: Q3 – A.
segments.tr: Q3 – A.

segments.src: A memorable joke can overshadow the brand (the "vampire effect"), so viewers enjoy the ad but can't recall who it was for.*
segments.tr: 기억에 남는 농담이 브랜드를 가려버릴 수 있어(“뱀파이어 효과”), 시청자는 광고를 즐기면서도 그것이 무슨 광고였는지 떠올리지 못합니다.*

zh.title: [消费者心理学 #6] 为什么搞笑广告能卖薯片却卖不动汽车：说服究竟如何运作

segments.src: > An ad persuades in different ways depending on how much you care and how closely you're paying attention. Fear and humor can both work, but only when they're used carefully.
segments.tr: > 广告以不同方式说服你，取决于你有多在意、多专注地留意它。恐惧和幽默都可能奏效，但前提是要谨慎使用。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: Every ad is trying to change something in your head, whether that's a belief ("this brand is reliable"), a feeling ("this brand is fun"), or a behavior ("buy now").
segments.tr: 每一则广告都在试图改变你脑中的某些东西，无论是信念（“这个品牌很可靠”）、情感（“这个品牌很有趣”），还是行为（“立即购买”）。

segments.src: Persuasion is the process of making that change.
segments.tr: 说服就是促成这种改变的过程。

segments.src: Researchers have spent decades studying **why some messages work and others don't.**
segments.tr: 几十年来，研究者一直在研究**为什么有些信息奏效，有些却不然。**

segments.src: The Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM)**
segments.tr: 精细可能性模型（ELM）**

segments.src: Psychologists Richard Petty and John Cacioppo proposed the ELM in the 1980s.
segments.tr: 心理学家理查德·佩蒂（Richard Petty）和约翰·卡乔波（John Cacioppo）在 1980 年代提出了 ELM。

segments.src: Its main idea is that people process a persuasive message along one of two routes:
segments.tr: 它的核心思想是：人们处理说服性信息时会沿着两条路径之一进行：

segments.src: - **Central route.** You think carefully about the message: Is the evidence good? Do the claims hold up? People take this route when they are **motivated** (the decision matters to them) and **able** (they have the time, attention, and knowledge). Attitudes formed this way tend to last longer and are harder to change.
segments.tr: - **中心路径。** 你会仔细思考这条信息：证据是否可靠？主张能否站得住脚？当人们既**有动机**（这个决定对他们很重要）又**有能力**（有时间、注意力和相关知识）时，就会走这条路径。以这种方式形成的态度往往更持久，也更难改变。

segments.src: - **Peripheral route.** You rely on shortcuts such as an attractive spokesperson, a catchy jingle, a celebrity, or simply "lots of people bought it." People take this route when they're distracted, in a hurry, or don't care much. Attitudes formed this way can shift quickly, and they can fade just as quickly.
segments.tr: - **边缘路径。** 你依赖一些捷径，例如有魅力的代言人、朗朗上口的广告曲、名人，或者只是“很多人都买了”。当人们分心、匆忙或不太在意时，就会走这条路径。以这种方式形成的态度可能迅速改变，也可能同样迅速消退。

segments.src: "Elaboration" just means how much you think about the message.
segments.tr: “精细化”（elaboration）只是指你对信息思考的程度。

segments.src: The same ad can persuade one person through careful reasoning and another through a smiling face.
segments.tr: 同一则广告，可能让一个人通过仔细推理而被说服，却让另一个人因为一张笑脸而被说服。

segments.src: Fear appeals**
segments.tr: 恐惧诉求（Fear appeals）**

segments.src: A fear appeal shows a threat, such as illness, an accident, or financial loss, to motivate action.
segments.tr: 恐惧诉求通过展示威胁（例如疾病、事故或经济损失）来促使人们采取行动。

segments.src: Research, including Kim Witte's Extended Parallel Process Model, suggests that fear works only when it comes with **efficacy**: the audience has to believe there's a clear, doable step that will actually protect them.
segments.tr: 包括 Kim Witte 的扩展平行过程模型在内的研究表明，恐惧只有伴随**效能感**时才会起作用：受众必须相信存在一个清晰、可行的步骤，能够真正保护自己。

segments.src: When a message has high threat and low efficacy, people often push it away instead of acting on it.
segments.tr: 当信息带来的威胁高而效能感低时，人们往往会排斥它，而不是据此采取行动。

segments.src: They avoid the topic, doubt the source, or tell themselves "it won't happen to me."
segments.tr: 他们会回避这个话题、怀疑信息来源，或者告诉自己“这种事不会发生在我身上”。

segments.src: Scaring people harder doesn't automatically make the message work better.
segments.tr: 把人吓得更厉害，并不会自动让信息更有效。

segments.src: Humor appeals**
segments.tr: 幽默诉求（Humor appeals）**

segments.src: Humor grabs attention and makes people like the ad, and that good feeling can rub off on the brand.
segments.tr: 幽默能抓住注意力，让人们喜欢这则广告，而这种良好的感受可能会转移到品牌上。

segments.src: It has downsides, though:
segments.tr: 不过它也有缺点：

segments.src: - It can **distract** viewers from the actual product information.
segments.tr: - 它可能会**分散**观众对产品实际信息的注意力。

segments.src: - People may remember the joke and forget the brand, which practitioners sometimes call the "vampire effect."
segments.tr: - 人们可能记住了笑话，却忘了品牌，业内人士有时称之为“吸血鬼效应”（vampire effect）。

segments.src: - It usually works better for **familiar, low-risk, low-involvement products** (snacks, soda, fast food) than for complex or high-stakes purchases.
segments.tr: - 它通常更适用于**熟悉、低风险、低卷入度的产品**（零食、汽水、快餐），而不太适用于复杂或高风险的购买。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活中

segments.src: Jordan, who lives in Columbus, Ohio, is watching football on Sunday.
segments.tr: Jordan 住在俄亥俄州的哥伦布市，周日正在看橄榄球比赛。

segments.src: During a commercial break, a goofy car insurance ad gets a laugh.
segments.tr: 广告插播时，一则傻乎乎的汽车保险广告逗得他笑了出来。

segments.src: Jordan isn't shopping for insurance right now, so the joke and the memorable mascot are basically all that sticks.
segments.tr: Jordan 现在并没有买保险的打算，所以留下来的基本只有那个笑话和令人印象深刻的吉祥物。

segments.src: That's the **peripheral route**, and it worked: the brand name is now in Jordan's head.
segments.tr: 这就是**边缘路径**，而且它起了作用：品牌名称已经留在了 Jordan 的脑海里。

segments.src: Three weeks later, Jordan's policy is up for renewal, and the quotes are around $1,400 a year.
segments.tr: 三周后，Jordan 的保单到期需要续保，报价约为每年 1,400 美元。

segments.src: Now Jordan is motivated and sits down with a laptop to compare deductibles, liability limits, and customer reviews.
segments.tr: 这一次 Jordan 有了动机，于是坐下来用笔记本电脑比较免赔额、责任限额和客户评价。

segments.src: That's the **central route**.
segments.tr: 这就是**中心路径**。

segments.src: A funny ad won't close this sale.
segments.tr: 一则搞笑广告无法促成这笔交易。

segments.src: Clear numbers and believable claims will.
segments.tr: 清晰的数字和可信的主张才能做到。

segments.src: Later that week, Jordan sees a public service ad from the CDC's long-running "Tips From Former Smokers" campaign, which features real people living with smoking-related illnesses.
segments.tr: 那周晚些时候，Jordan 看到了美国疾控中心（CDC）长期开展的“前吸烟者的建议”（Tips From Former Smokers）公益广告，片中是真实的、患有吸烟相关疾病的人。

segments.src: The ad is frightening, but it ends with a concrete step: call 1-800-QUIT-NOW for free help.
segments.tr: 这则广告令人恐惧，但结尾给出了一个具体行动：拨打 1-800-QUIT-NOW 获取免费帮助。

segments.src: It pairs **threat with efficacy**, which is how a fear appeal is supposed to be built.
segments.tr: 它把**威胁与效能感**结合在一起，这正是恐惧诉求应有的构建方式。

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. According to the ELM, people process ads through a careful **central route** or a shortcut-based **peripheral route**, depending on their motivation and ability.
segments.tr: 1. 根据 ELM，人们会依据自身的动机和能力，通过仔细的**中心路径**或基于捷径的**边缘路径**来处理广告。

segments.src: 2. **Fear appeals** work best when the threat comes with a clear, doable solution. Fear without a way out tends to cause avoidance.
segments.tr: 2. 当威胁附带清晰、可行的解决方案时，**恐惧诉求**效果最好。没有出路的恐惧往往导致回避。

segments.src: 3. **Humor** boosts attention and liking but can bury the message. It fits low-involvement products better than high-stakes ones.
segments.tr: 3. **幽默**能提升注意力和好感，但也可能掩盖信息本身。它比高风险产品更适合低卷入度产品。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自测题

segments.src: **Q1.** According to the ELM, which situation makes the central route most likely?
segments.tr: **Q1.** 根据 ELM，哪种情况最有可能引发中心路径？

segments.src: - A) Scrolling past an ad while chatting with friends
segments.tr: - A) 和朋友聊天时划过一则广告

segments.src: - B) Researching a new $30,000 car you plan to buy next month
segments.tr: - B) 正在研究下个月打算购买的一辆 3 万美元的汽车

segments.src: - C) Hearing a jingle on the radio while driving
segments.tr: - C) 开车时在广播里听到一段广告曲

segments.src: - D) Seeing a celebrity holding a soda can
segments.tr: - D) 看到名人手里拿着一罐汽水

segments.src: **Q2.** (True/False) The scarier a fear appeal is, the more effective it always becomes.
segments.tr: **Q2.**（正确/错误）恐惧诉求越吓人，效果就一定越好。

segments.src: **Q3.** Which is a known risk of humor appeals?
segments.tr: **Q3.** 下列哪一项是幽默诉求已知的风险？

segments.src: - A) Viewers remember the joke but forget the brand
segments.tr: - A) 观众记住了笑话，却忘了品牌

segments.src: - B) Humor always lowers attention
segments.tr: - B) 幽默总会降低注意力

segments.src: - C) Humor only works for expensive products
segments.tr: - C) 幽默只对昂贵的产品有效

segments.src: - D) Humor makes ads illegal in some states
segments.tr: - D) 幽默会让广告在某些州变成违法

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM):** A theory stating that persuasion happens through either careful thinking (central route) or mental shortcuts (peripheral route).
segments.tr: - **精细可能性模型（ELM）：** 一种理论，认为说服要么通过仔细思考（中心路径），要么通过心理捷径（边缘路径）发生。

segments.src: - **Central route:** Being persuaded by carefully evaluating the arguments and evidence in a message.
segments.tr: - **中心路径：** 通过仔细评估信息中的论点和证据而被说服。

segments.src: - **Peripheral route:** Being persuaded by surface cues such as attractiveness, celebrity, music, or popularity.
segments.tr: - **边缘路径：** 通过吸引力、名人、音乐或受欢迎程度等表面线索而被说服。

segments.src: - **Fear appeal:** A message that highlights a threat to motivate protective action. It works best when paired with a clear solution (efficacy).
segments.tr: - **恐惧诉求：** 强调威胁以促使人们采取保护性行动的信息。与清晰的解决方案（效能感）搭配时效果最好。

segments.src: - **Humor appeal:** Using comedy in a message to capture attention and build positive feelings toward a brand.
segments.tr: - **幽默诉求：** 在信息中运用喜剧来吸引注意力，并建立对品牌的积极情感。

segments.src: *Answers: Q1 – B.
segments.tr: *答案：Q1 – B。

segments.src: A big, personally important purchase gives you both the motivation and the time to weigh the details, which is the central route.
segments.tr: 一次金额大、与个人切身相关的购买，既提供了动机，也提供了仔细权衡细节的时间，这正是中心路径。

segments.src: Q2 – False.
segments.tr: Q2 – 错误。

segments.src: Without a believable, doable solution, very strong fear often leads people to avoid or reject the message.
segments.tr: 没有可信、可行的解决方案时，非常强烈的恐惧往往让人回避或拒绝信息。

segments.src: Q3 – A.
segments.tr: Q3 – A。

segments.src: A memorable joke can overshadow the brand (the "vampire effect"), so viewers enjoy the ad but can't recall who it was for.*
segments.tr: 令人难忘的笑话可能会盖过品牌（“吸血鬼效应”），因此观众喜欢广告，却想不起它是为哪个品牌做的。*

hi.title: [Consumer Psychology #6] एक मज़ेदार विज्ञापन चिप्स क्यों बेच सकता है, कार क्यों नहीं: मनाना असल में कैसे काम करता है

segments.src: > An ad persuades in different ways depending on how much you care and how closely you're paying attention. Fear and humor can both work, but only when they're used carefully.
segments.tr: > किसी विज्ञापन का असर इस बात पर निर्भर करता है कि आप उसकी कितनी परवाह करते हैं और उस पर कितना ध्यान देते हैं। डर और हास्य, दोनों काम कर सकते हैं, लेकिन तभी जब उन्हें सावधानी से इस्तेमाल किया जाए।

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: Every ad is trying to change something in your head, whether that's a belief ("this brand is reliable"), a feeling ("this brand is fun"), or a behavior ("buy now").
segments.tr: हर विज्ञापन आपके मन में कुछ बदलने की कोशिश करता है, चाहे वह कोई विश्वास हो ("यह ब्रांड भरोसेमंद है"), कोई भावना हो ("यह ब्रांड मज़ेदार है"), या कोई व्यवहार हो ("अभी खरीदें")।

segments.src: Persuasion is the process of making that change.
segments.tr: मनाना (Persuasion) वह प्रक्रिया है जिससे यह बदलाव लाया जाता है।

segments.src: Researchers have spent decades studying **why some messages work and others don't.**
segments.tr: शोधकर्ताओं ने दशकों तक इस बात का अध्ययन किया है कि **कुछ संदेश क्यों काम करते हैं और कुछ क्यों नहीं।**

segments.src: The Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM)**
segments.tr: विस्तार-संभावना मॉडल (ELM)**

segments.src: Psychologists Richard Petty and John Cacioppo proposed the ELM in the 1980s.
segments.tr: मनोवैज्ञानिक रिचर्ड पेटी और जॉन कैसिओपो ने 1980 के दशक में ELM का प्रस्ताव रखा था।

segments.src: Its main idea is that people process a persuasive message along one of two routes:
segments.tr: इसका मुख्य विचार यह है कि लोग किसी मनाने वाले संदेश को दो मार्गों में से किसी एक से संसाधित करते हैं:

segments.src: - **Central route.** You think carefully about the message: Is the evidence good? Do the claims hold up? People take this route when they are **motivated** (the decision matters to them) and **able** (they have the time, attention, and knowledge). Attitudes formed this way tend to last longer and are harder to change.
segments.tr: - **केंद्रीय मार्ग।** आप संदेश के बारे में ध्यान से सोचते हैं: क्या प्रमाण अच्छे हैं? क्या दावे टिकते हैं? लोग यह मार्ग तब अपनाते हैं जब वे **प्रेरित** (फैसला उनके लिए मायने रखता है) और **सक्षम** (उनके पास समय, ध्यान और जानकारी है) होते हैं। इस तरह बनने वाले रवैये आमतौर पर अधिक समय तक टिकते हैं और उन्हें बदलना कठिन होता है।

segments.src: - **Peripheral route.** You rely on shortcuts such as an attractive spokesperson, a catchy jingle, a celebrity, or simply "lots of people bought it." People take this route when they're distracted, in a hurry, or don't care much. Attitudes formed this way can shift quickly, and they can fade just as quickly.
segments.tr: - **परिधीय मार्ग।** आप शॉर्टकट पर भरोसा करते हैं, जैसे कोई आकर्षक प्रवक्ता, कोई याद रह जाने वाली धुन, कोई मशहूर हस्ती, या बस यह बात कि "बहुत लोगों ने इसे खरीदा है।" लोग यह मार्ग तब अपनाते हैं जब उनका ध्यान बँटा होता है, वे जल्दी में होते हैं, या उन्हें ज़्यादा परवाह नहीं होती। इस तरह बने रवैये तेज़ी से बदल सकते हैं, और उतनी ही तेज़ी से फीके भी पड़ सकते हैं।

segments.src: "Elaboration" just means how much you think about the message.
segments.tr: "विस्तार" (Elaboration) का मतलब बस इतना है कि आप संदेश के बारे में कितना सोचते हैं।

segments.src: The same ad can persuade one person through careful reasoning and another through a smiling face.
segments.tr: वही विज्ञापन एक व्यक्ति को सावधानीपूर्वक तर्क से मना सकता है और दूसरे को मुस्कुराते चेहरे से।

segments.src: Fear appeals**
segments.tr: भय-अपील (Fear appeals)**

segments.src: A fear appeal shows a threat, such as illness, an accident, or financial loss, to motivate action.
segments.tr: भय-अपील किसी खतरे को दिखाती है, जैसे बीमारी, दुर्घटना या आर्थिक नुकसान, ताकि कार्रवाई के लिए प्रेरित किया जा सके।

segments.src: Research, including Kim Witte's Extended Parallel Process Model, suggests that fear works only when it comes with **efficacy**: the audience has to believe there's a clear, doable step that will actually protect them.
segments.tr: Kim Witte के Extended Parallel Process Model सहित शोध बताता है कि डर तभी काम करता है जब उसके साथ **प्रभावकारिता (efficacy)** हो: दर्शक को यह विश्वास होना चाहिए कि एक स्पष्ट, करने योग्य कदम मौजूद है जो सच में उसकी रक्षा करेगा।

segments.src: When a message has high threat and low efficacy, people often push it away instead of acting on it.
segments.tr: जब किसी संदेश में खतरा ऊँचा और प्रभावकारिता कम होती है, तो लोग अक्सर उसे परे धकेल देते हैं, कार्रवाई करने के बजाय।

segments.src: They avoid the topic, doubt the source, or tell themselves "it won't happen to me."
segments.tr: वे विषय से कतराते हैं, स्रोत पर शक करते हैं, या खुद से कहते हैं कि "ऐसा मेरे साथ नहीं होगा।"

segments.src: Scaring people harder doesn't automatically make the message work better.
segments.tr: लोगों को और ज़्यादा डराने से संदेश अपने आप बेहतर काम नहीं करने लगता।

segments.src: Humor appeals**
segments.tr: हास्य-अपील (Humor appeals)**

segments.src: Humor grabs attention and makes people like the ad, and that good feeling can rub off on the brand.
segments.tr: हास्य ध्यान खींचता है और लोगों को विज्ञापन पसंद आता है, और वह अच्छा एहसास ब्रांड पर भी चढ़ सकता है।

segments.src: It has downsides, though:
segments.tr: लेकिन इसके नुकसान भी हैं:

segments.src: - It can **distract** viewers from the actual product information.
segments.tr: - यह दर्शकों का ध्यान असली उत्पाद की जानकारी से **भटका** सकता है।

segments.src: - People may remember the joke and forget the brand, which practitioners sometimes call the "vampire effect."
segments.tr: - लोग चुटकुला याद रख सकते हैं और ब्रांड भूल सकते हैं, जिसे विशेषज्ञ कभी-कभी "वैम्पायर इफ़ेक्ट" कहते हैं।

segments.src: - It usually works better for **familiar, low-risk, low-involvement products** (snacks, soda, fast food) than for complex or high-stakes purchases.
segments.tr: - यह आमतौर पर **जाने-पहचाने, कम जोखिम वाले, कम सोच-विचार वाले उत्पादों** (स्नैक्स, सोडा, फास्ट फूड) के लिए जटिल या बड़े दांव वाली खरीदारी की तुलना में बेहतर काम करता है।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी में

segments.src: Jordan, who lives in Columbus, Ohio, is watching football on Sunday.
segments.tr: जॉर्डन, जो कोलंबस, ओहायो में रहते हैं, रविवार को फुटबॉल देख रहे हैं।

segments.src: During a commercial break, a goofy car insurance ad gets a laugh.
segments.tr: विज्ञापन के ब्रेक के दौरान, एक मज़ाकिया कार बीमा विज्ञापन पर हँसी आ जाती है।

segments.src: Jordan isn't shopping for insurance right now, so the joke and the memorable mascot are basically all that sticks.
segments.tr: जॉर्डन अभी बीमा नहीं खरीद रहे, इसलिए बस वह चुटकुला और यादगार मैस्कॉट ही मन में टिकते हैं।

segments.src: That's the **peripheral route**, and it worked: the brand name is now in Jordan's head.
segments.tr: यह **परिधीय मार्ग** है, और यह काम कर गया: ब्रांड का नाम अब जॉर्डन के मन में है।

segments.src: Three weeks later, Jordan's policy is up for renewal, and the quotes are around $1,400 a year.
segments.tr: तीन हफ्ते बाद, जॉर्डन की पॉलिसी के नवीनीकरण का समय आता है, और कोट लगभग $1,400 प्रति वर्ष के आसपास हैं।

segments.src: Now Jordan is motivated and sits down with a laptop to compare deductibles, liability limits, and customer reviews.
segments.tr: अब जॉर्डन प्रेरित हैं और लैपटॉप लेकर कटौती (deductibles), देयता सीमा (liability limits) और ग्राहक समीक्षाओं की तुलना करने बैठते हैं।

segments.src: That's the **central route**.
segments.tr: यह **केंद्रीय मार्ग** है।

segments.src: A funny ad won't close this sale.
segments.tr: कोई मज़ेदार विज्ञापन यह बिक्री पक्की नहीं करेगा।

segments.src: Clear numbers and believable claims will.

es.title: [Psicología del consumidor #6] ¿Por qué un anuncio gracioso puede vender papas fritas pero no un auto? Cómo funciona realmente la persuasión

segments.src: > An ad persuades in different ways depending on how much you care and how closely you're paying attention. Fear and humor can both work, but only when they're used carefully.
segments.tr: > Un anuncio persuade de distintas formas según cuánto te importe el tema y qué tan de cerca prestes atención. El miedo y el humor pueden funcionar, pero solo cuando se usan con cuidado.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: Every ad is trying to change something in your head, whether that's a belief ("this brand is reliable"), a feeling ("this brand is fun"), or a behavior ("buy now").
segments.tr: Todo anuncio intenta cambiar algo en tu mente, ya sea una creencia (“esta marca es confiable”), un sentimiento (“esta marca es divertida”) o un comportamiento (“compra ahora”).

segments.src: Persuasion is the process of making that change.
segments.tr: La persuasión es el proceso de lograr ese cambio.

segments.src: Researchers have spent decades studying **why some messages work and others don't.**
segments.tr: Durante décadas, los investigadores han estudiado **por qué algunos mensajes funcionan y otros no.**

segments.src: The Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM)**
segments.tr: El Modelo de Probabilidad de Elaboración (ELM)**

segments.src: Psychologists Richard Petty and John Cacioppo proposed the ELM in the 1980s.
segments.tr: Los psicólogos Richard Petty y John Cacioppo propusieron el ELM en los años ochenta.

segments.src: Its main idea is that people process a persuasive message along one of two routes:
segments.tr: Su idea central es que las personas procesan un mensaje persuasivo por una de dos rutas:

segments.src: - **Central route.** You think carefully about the message: Is the evidence good? Do the claims hold up? People take this route when they are **motivated** (the decision matters to them) and **able** (they have the time, attention, and knowledge). Attitudes formed this way tend to last longer and are harder to change.
segments.tr: - **Ruta central.** Piensas detenidamente en el mensaje: ¿es buena la evidencia? ¿Se sostienen las afirmaciones? Las personas siguen esta ruta cuando están **motivadas** (la decisión les importa) y **capacitadas** (tienen tiempo, atención y conocimiento). Las actitudes formadas así tienden a durar más y son más difíciles de cambiar.

segments.src: - **Peripheral route.** You rely on shortcuts such as an attractive spokesperson, a catchy jingle, a celebrity, or simply "lots of people bought it." People take this route when they're distracted, in a hurry, or don't care much. Attitudes formed this way can shift quickly, and they can fade just as quickly.
segments.tr: - **Ruta periférica.** Te basas en atajos como un portavoz atractivo, una melodía pegajosa, una celebridad o simplemente “mucha gente lo compró”. Las personas siguen esta ruta cuando están distraídas, apuradas o no les importa demasiado. Las actitudes formadas así pueden cambiar rápido, y también desvanecerse igual de rápido.

segments.src: "Elaboration" just means how much you think about the message.
segments.tr: “Elaboración” solo significa cuánto piensas en el mensaje.

segments.src: The same ad can persuade one person through careful reasoning and another through a smiling face.
segments.tr: El mismo anuncio puede persuadir a una persona mediante un razonamiento cuidadoso y a otra mediante una cara sonriente.

segments.src: Fear appeals**
segments.tr: Apelaciones al miedo**

segments.src: A fear appeal shows a threat, such as illness, an accident, or financial loss, to motivate action.
segments.tr: Una apelación al miedo muestra una amenaza, como una enfermedad, un accidente o una pérdida económica, para motivar una acción.

segments.src: Research, including Kim Witte's Extended Parallel Process Model, suggests that fear works only when it comes with **efficacy**: the audience has to believe there's a clear, doable step that will actually protect them.
segments.tr: La investigación, incluido el Modelo Extendido de Proceso Paralelo de Kim Witte, sugiere que el miedo solo funciona cuando va acompañado de **eficacia**: la audiencia debe creer que existe un paso claro y factible que realmente la protegerá.

segments.src: When a message has high threat and low efficacy, people often push it away instead of acting on it.
segments.tr: Cuando un mensaje tiene mucha amenaza y poca eficacia, la gente suele rechazarlo en lugar de actuar.

segments.src: They avoid the topic, doubt the source, or tell themselves "it won't happen to me."
segments.tr: Evitan el tema, desconfían de la fuente o se dicen a sí mismos “a mí no me va a pasar”.

segments.src: Scaring people harder doesn't automatically make the message work better.
segments.tr: Asustar a la gente con más fuerza no hace automáticamente que el mensaje funcione mejor.

segments.src: Humor appeals**
segments.tr: Apelaciones al humor**

segments.src: Humor grabs attention and makes people like the ad, and that good feeling can rub off on the brand.
segments.tr: El humor capta la atención y hace que la gente simpatice con el anuncio, y esa buena sensación puede extenderse a la marca.

segments.src: It has downsides, though:
segments.tr: Sin embargo, tiene desventajas:

segments.src: - It can **distract** viewers from the actual product information.
segments.tr: - Puede **distraer** al espectador de la información real sobre el producto.

segments.src: - People may remember the joke and forget the brand, which practitioners sometimes call the "vampire effect."
segments.tr: - La gente puede recordar el chiste y olvidar la marca, lo que los profesionales a veces llaman el “efecto vampiro”.

segments.src: - It usually works better for **familiar, low-risk, low-involvement products** (snacks, soda, fast food) than for complex or high-stakes purchases.
segments.tr: - Suele funcionar mejor con **productos familiares, de bajo riesgo y baja implicación** (botanas, refrescos, comida rápida) que con compras complejas o de alto riesgo.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: Jordan, who lives in Columbus, Ohio, is watching football on Sunday.
segments.tr: Jordan, que vive en Columbus, Ohio, ve fútbol americano el domingo.

segments.src: During a commercial break, a goofy car insurance ad gets a laugh.
segments.tr: Durante una pausa comercial, un anuncio tonto de seguros de auto arranca una risa.

segments.src: Jordan isn't shopping for insurance right now, so the joke and the memorable mascot are basically all that sticks.
segments.tr: Jordan no está buscando un seguro en este momento, así que lo único que se queda es el chiste y la mascota memorable.

segments.src: That's the **peripheral route**, and it worked: the brand name is now in Jordan's head.
segments.tr: Esa es la **ruta periférica**, y funcionó: el nombre de la marca ya está en la cabeza de Jordan.

segments.tr: Esa es la **ruta central**.

segments.src: A funny ad won't close this sale.
segments.tr: Un anuncio gracioso no cerrará esta venta.

segments.src: Clear numbers and believable claims will.
segments.tr: Lo harán las cifras claras y las afirmaciones creíbles.

segments.tr: نموذج احتمالية التفصيل (ELM)**

segments.src: Psychologists Richard Petty and John Cacioppo proposed the ELM in the 1980s.
segments.tr: اقترح عالما النفس ريتشارد بيتي وجون كاسيوبو نموذج ELM في الثمانينيات.

segments.src: Its main idea is that people process a persuasive message along one of two routes:
segments.tr: فكرته الأساسية أن الناس يعالجون الرسالة الإقناعية عبر أحد مسارين:

segments.src: - **Central route.** You think carefully about the message: Is the evidence good? Do the claims hold up? People take this route when they are **motivated** (the decision matters to them) and **able** (they have the time, attention, and knowledge). Attitudes formed this way tend to last longer and are harder to change.
segments.tr: - **المسار المركزي.** تفكر في الرسالة بعناية: هل الأدلة جيدة؟ هل الادعاءات صحيحة؟ يسلك الناس هذا المسار عندما يكونون **متحفزين** (القرار يهمهم) و**قادرين** (لديهم الوقت والانتباه والمعرفة). المواقف التي تتكون بهذه الطريقة تميل إلى الدوام أطول وتكون أصعب في التغيير.

segments.src: - **Peripheral route.** You rely on shortcuts such as an attractive spokesperson, a catchy jingle, a celebrity, or simply "lots of people bought it." People take this route when they're distracted, in a hurry, or don't care much. Attitudes formed this way can shift quickly, and they can fade just as quickly.
segments.tr: - **المسار الطرفي.** تعتمد على اختصارات مثل متحدث جذاب، أو لحن دعائي يعلق في الذهن، أو مشهور، أو مجرد “أن كثيرين اشتروه”. يسلك الناس هذا المسار عندما يكونون مشتتين أو في عجلة أو لا يهتمون كثيراً. المواقف التي تتكون بهذه الطريقة قد تتغير بسرعة، وقد تتلاشى بالسرعة نفسها.

segments.src: "Elaboration" just means how much you think about the message.
segments.tr: “التفصيل” يعني فقط مقدار ما تفكر فيه في الرسالة.

segments.src: The same ad can persuade one person through careful reasoning and another through a smiling face.
segments.tr: قد يقنع الإعلان نفسه شخصاً عبر تفكير متأنٍ، ويقنع آخر عبر وجه مبتسم.

segments.src: Fear appeals**
segments.tr: نداءات الخوف**

segments.src: A fear appeal shows a threat, such as illness, an accident, or financial loss, to motivate action.
segments.tr: نداء الخوف يعرض تهديداً، مثل المرض أو حادث أو خسارة مالية، لدفعك إلى التحرك.

segments.src: Research, including Kim Witte's Extended Parallel Process Model, suggests that fear works only when it comes with **efficacy**: the audience has to believe there's a clear, doable step that will actually protect them.
segments.tr: تشير الأبحاث، ومنها نموذج Kim Witte للمعالجة المتوازية الموسّعة (Extended Parallel Process Model)، إلى أن الخوف يعمل فقط عندما يقترن بـ**الفعالية**: يجب أن يعتقد الجمهور أن هناك خطوة واضحة وممكنة التنفيذ ستحميه فعلاً.

segments.src: When a message has high threat and low efficacy, people often push it away instead of acting on it.
segments.tr: عندما تحمل الرسالة تهديداً مرتفعاً وفعالية منخفضة، يدفع الناس الرسالة بعيداً غالباً بدلاً من التصرف بناءً عليها.

segments.src: They avoid the topic, doubt the source, or tell themselves "it won't happen to me."
segments.tr: يتجنبون الموضوع، أو يشككون في المصدر، أو يقولون لأنفسهم “لن يحدث لي”.

segments.src: Scaring people harder doesn't automatically make the message work better.
segments.tr: تخويف الناس بشدة أكبر لا يجعل الرسالة أكثر نجاعة تلقائياً.

segments.src: Humor appeals**
segments.tr: نداءات الفكاهة**

segments.src: Humor grabs attention and makes people like the ad, and that good feeling can rub off on the brand.
segments.tr: الفكاهة تجذب الانتباه وتجعل الناس يحبون الإعلان، وقد ينتقل هذا الشعور الجيد إلى العلامة التجارية.

segments.src: It has downsides, though:
segments.tr: لكن لها عيوباً أيضاً:

segments.src: - It can **distract** viewers from the actual product information.
segments.tr: - يمكن أن **تشتت** المشاهد عن معلومات المنتج الفعلية.

segments.src: - People may remember the joke and forget the brand, which practitioners sometimes call the "vampire effect."
segments.tr: - قد يتذكر الناس النكتة وينسون العلامة التجارية، وهو ما يسميه الممارسون أحياناً “تأثير مصاصي الدماء”.

segments.src: - It usually works better for **familiar, low-risk, low-involvement products** (snacks, soda, fast food) than for complex or high-stakes purchases.
segments.tr: - عادةً ما تعمل بشكل أفضل مع **المنتجات المألوفة منخفضة المخاطر ومنخفضة الانخراط** (الوجبات الخفيفة، والمشروبات الغازية، والوجبات السريعة) أكثر من المشتريات المعقدة أو عالية المخاطر.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: Jordan, who lives in Columbus, Ohio, is watching football on Sunday.
segments.tr: جوردان، الذي يعيش في كولومبوس بولاية أوهايو، يشاهد كرة القدم يوم الأحد.

segments.src: During a commercial break, a goofy car insurance ad gets a laugh.
segments.tr: خلال فاصل إعلاني، يضحكه إعلان تأمين سيارات مرح.

segments.src: Jordan isn't shopping for insurance right now, so the joke and the memorable mascot are basically all that sticks.
segments.tr: جوردان ليس في وضع تسوق للتأمين الآن، لذلك لا يعلق في الذهن عملياً إلا النكتة والشخصية الكرتونية المميزة.

segments.src: That's the **peripheral route**, and it worked: the brand name is now in Jordan's head.
segments.tr: هذا هو **المسار الطرفي**، وقد نجح: اسم العلامة التجارية صار في ذهن جوردان.

segments.src: Three weeks later, Jordan's policy is up for renewal, and the quotes are around $1,400 a year.
segments.tr: بعد ثلاثة أسابيع، يحين موعد تجديد وثيقة جوردان، وعروض الأسعار تدور حول 1,400 دولار سنوياً.

segments.src: Now Jordan is motivated and sits down with a laptop to compare deductibles, liability limits, and customer reviews.
segments.tr: الآن يصبح جوردان متحفزاً، فيجلس أمام حاسوب محمول ليقارن الاقتطاعات (deductibles) وحدود المسؤولية وتقييمات العملاء.

segments.src: That's the **central route**.
segments.tr: هذا هو **المسار المركزي**.

segments.src: A funny ad won't close this sale.
segments.tr: الإعلان المضحك لن يغلق هذه الصفقة.

segments.src: Clear numbers and believable claims will.
segments.tr: الأرقام الواضحة والادعاءات القابلة للتصديق هي التي ستفعل ذلك.

segments.src: Later that week, Jordan sees a public service ad from the CDC's long-running "Tips From Former Smokers" campaign, which features real people living with smoking-related illnesses.
segments.tr: في وقت لاحق من ذلك الأسبوع، يرى جوردان إعلاناً للخدمة العامة من حملة “Tips From Former Smokers” الطويلة الأمد التابعة لمراكز مكافحة الأمراض والوقاية منها (CDC)، ويظهر فيه أشخاص حقيقيون يعيشون مع أمراض مرتبطة بالتدخين.

segments.src: The ad is frightening, but it ends with a concrete step: call 1-800-QUIT-NOW for free help.
segments.tr: الإعلان مخيف، لكنه ينتهي بخطوة ملموسة: اتصل بالرقم 1-800-QUIT-NOW للحصول على مساعدة مجانية.

segments.src: It pairs **threat with efficacy**, which is how a fear appeal is supposed to be built.
segments.tr: إنه يجمع **التهديد مع الفعالية**، وهكذا يُفترض أن يُبنى نداء الخوف.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## ملخص في ثلاثة أسطر

segments.src: 1. According to the ELM, people process ads through a careful **central route** or a shortcut-based **peripheral route**, depending on their motivation and ability.
segments.tr: 1. وفقاً لنموذج ELM، يعالج الناس الإعلانات عبر **مسار مركزي** متأنٍ أو **مسار طرفي** قائم على الاختصارات، حسب دافعيتهم وقدرتهم.

segments.src: 2. **Fear appeals** work best when the threat comes with a clear, doable solution. Fear without a way out tends to cause avoidance.
segments.tr: 2. **نداءات الخوف** تعمل بأفضل شكل عندما يقترن التهديد بحل واضح وممكن التنفيذ. الخوف دون مخرج يميل إلى إحداث التجنب.

segments.src: 3. **Humor** boosts attention and liking but can bury the message. It fits low-involvement products better than high-stakes ones.
segments.tr: 3. **الفكاهة** تعزز الانتباه والإعجاب لكنها قد تطمس الرسالة. وهي أنسب للمنتجات منخفضة الانخراط منها للمنتجات عالية المخاطر.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ اختبار ذاتي

segments.src: **Q1.** According to the ELM, which situation makes the central route most likely?
segments.tr: **س1.** وفقاً لنموذج ELM، أي موقف يجعل المسار المركزي أكثر احتمالاً؟

segments.src: - A) Scrolling past an ad while chatting with friends
segments.tr: - أ) تمرير إعلان أثناء الدردشة مع الأصدقاء

segments.src: - B) Researching a new $30,000 car you plan to buy next month
segments.tr: - ب) البحث عن سيارة جديدة بقيمة 30,000 دولار تخطط لشرائها الشهر القادم

segments.src: - C) Hearing a jingle on the radio while driving
segments.tr: - ج) سماع لحن دعائي في الراديو أثناء القيادة

segments.src: - D) Seeing a celebrity holding a soda can
segments.tr: - د) رؤية مشهور يمسك علبة مشروب غازي

segments.src: **Q2.** (True/False) The scarier a fear appeal is, the more effective it always becomes.
segments.tr: **س2.** (صح/خطأ) كلما كان نداء الخوف أكثر إرعاباً، أصبح أكثر فعالية دائماً.

segments.src: **Q3.** Which is a known risk of humor appeals?
segments.tr: **س3.** أي مما يلي يُعد خطراً معروفاً لنداءات الفكاهة؟

segments.src: - A) Viewers remember the joke but forget the brand
segments.tr: - أ) يتذكر المشاهدون النكتة لكنهم ينسون العلامة التجارية

segments.src: - B) Humor always lowers attention
segments.tr: - ب) الفكاهة تخفض الانتباه دائماً

segments.src: - C) Humor only works for expensive products
segments.tr: - ج) الفكاهة تعمل فقط مع المنتجات باهظة الثمن

segments.src: - D) Humor makes ads illegal in some states
segments.tr: - د) الفكاهة تجعل الإعلانات غير قانونية في بعض الولايات

segments.tr: ## 📚 مصطلحات اليوم

segments.tr: - **نموذج احتمالية التفصيل (ELM):** نظرية تنص على أن الإقناع يحدث إما عبر تفكير متأنٍ (المسار المركزي) أو عبر اختصارات ذهنية (المسار الطرفي).

segments.src: - **Central route:** Being persuaded by carefully evaluating the arguments and evidence in a message.
segments.tr: - **المسار المركزي:** الاقتناع من خلال تقييم الحجج والأدلة في الرسالة بعناية.

segments.src: - **Peripheral route:** Being persuaded by surface cues such as attractiveness, celebrity, music, or popularity.
segments.tr: - **المسار الطرفي:** الاقتناع من خلال إشارات سطحية مثل الجاذبية، أو الشهرة، أو الموسيقى، أو الشعبية.

segments.tr: الشراء الكبير والمهم شخصياً يمنحك الدافعية والوقت لوزن التفاصيل، وهذا هو المسار المركزي.

fr.title: [Consumer Psychology #6] Pourquoi une pub drôle peut vendre des chips mais pas une voiture : comment la persuasion fonctionne vraiment

segments.src: > An ad persuades in different ways depending on how much you care and how closely you're paying attention. Fear and humor can both work, but only when they're used carefully.
segments.tr: > Une publicité persuade de différentes manières selon le degré d'intérêt que vous y portez et votre niveau d'attention. La peur et l'humour peuvent tous deux fonctionner, mais seulement lorsqu'ils sont utilisés avec précaution.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concept du jour

segments.src: Every ad is trying to change something in your head, whether that's a belief ("this brand is reliable"), a feeling ("this brand is fun"), or a behavior ("buy now").
segments.tr: Chaque publicité cherche à modifier quelque chose dans votre esprit, qu'il s'agisse d'une croyance (« cette marque est fiable »), d'un sentiment (« cette marque est amusante ») ou d'un comportement (« achetez maintenant »).

segments.src: Persuasion is the process of making that change.
segments.tr: La persuasion est le processus qui produit ce changement.

segments.src: Researchers have spent decades studying **why some messages work and others don't.**
segments.tr: Les chercheurs étudient depuis des décennies **pourquoi certains messages fonctionnent et d'autres non.**

segments.src: The Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM)**
segments.tr: Le modèle de probabilité d'élaboration (ELM)**

segments.src: Psychologists Richard Petty and John Cacioppo proposed the ELM in the 1980s.
segments.tr: Les psychologues Richard Petty et John Cacioppo ont proposé l'ELM dans les années 1980.

segments.src: Its main idea is that people process a persuasive message along one of two routes:
segments.tr: Son idée principale est que les gens traitent un message persuasif selon l'une de deux voies :

segments.src: - **Central route.** You think carefully about the message: Is the evidence good? Do the claims hold up? People take this route when they are **motivated** (the decision matters to them) and **able** (they have the time, attention, and knowledge). Attitudes formed this way tend to last longer and are harder to change.
segments.tr: - **Voie centrale.** Vous réfléchissez attentivement au message : les preuves sont-elles solides ? Les affirmations tiennent-elles la route ? Les gens empruntent cette voie lorsqu'ils sont **motivés** (la décision compte pour eux) et **capables** (ils ont le temps, l'attention et les connaissances nécessaires). Les attitudes formées de cette manière ont tendance à durer plus longtemps et sont plus difficiles à modifier.

segments.src: - **Peripheral route.** You rely on shortcuts such as an attractive spokesperson, a catchy jingle, a celebrity, or simply "lots of people bought it." People take this route when they're distracted, in a hurry, or don't care much. Attitudes formed this way can shift quickly, and they can fade just as quickly.
segments.tr: - **Voie périphérique.** Vous vous appuyez sur des raccourcis, comme un porte-parole séduisant, un jingle accrocheur, une célébrité ou simplement le fait que « beaucoup de gens l'ont acheté ». Les gens empruntent cette voie lorsqu'ils sont distraits, pressés ou peu concernés. Les attitudes formées ainsi peuvent changer rapidement, et elles peuvent aussi disparaître tout aussi vite.

segments.src: "Elaboration" just means how much you think about the message.
segments.tr: « Élaboration » signifie simplement le degré de réflexion que vous accordez au message.

segments.src: The same ad can persuade one person through careful reasoning and another through a smiling face.
segments.tr: La même publicité peut convaincre une personne par un raisonnement minutieux et une autre par un visage souriant.

segments.src: Fear appeals**
segments.tr: Les appels à la peur**

segments.src: A fear appeal shows a threat, such as illness, an accident, or financial loss, to motivate action.
segments.tr: Un appel à la peur montre une menace, comme une maladie, un accident ou une perte financière, afin de pousser à agir.

segments.src: Research, including Kim Witte's Extended Parallel Process Model, suggests that fear works only when it comes with **efficacy**: the audience has to believe there's a clear, doable step that will actually protect them.
segments.tr: Les recherches, notamment le modèle EPPM (Extended Parallel Process Model) de Kim Witte, suggèrent que la peur ne fonctionne que lorsqu'elle s'accompagne d'**efficacité** : le public doit croire qu'il existe une mesure claire et réalisable qui le protégera réellement.

segments.src: When a message has high threat and low efficacy, people often push it away instead of acting on it.
segments.tr: Lorsqu'un message présente une menace élevée et une efficacité faible, les gens le repoussent souvent au lieu d'agir.

segments.src: They avoid the topic, doubt the source, or tell themselves "it won't happen to me."
segments.tr: Ils évitent le sujet, doutent de la source ou se disent « ça ne m'arrivera pas ».

segments.src: Scaring people harder doesn't automatically make the message work better.
segments.tr: Effrayer davantage les gens ne rend pas automatiquement le message plus efficace.

segments.src: Humor appeals**
segments.tr: Les appels à l'humour**

segments.src: Humor grabs attention and makes people like the ad, and that good feeling can rub off on the brand.
segments.tr: L'humour capte l'attention et fait apprécier la publicité, et ce sentiment positif peut rejaillir sur la marque.

segments.src: It has downsides, though:
segments.tr: Il a toutefois des inconvénients :

segments.src: - It can **distract** viewers from the actual product information.
segments.tr: - Il peut **distraire** le spectateur des informations réelles sur le produit.

segments.src: - People may remember the joke and forget the brand, which practitioners sometimes call the "vampire effect."
segments.tr: - Les gens peuvent retenir la blague et oublier la marque, ce que les professionnels appellent parfois « l'effet vampire ».

segments.src: - It usually works better for **familiar, low-risk, low-involvement products** (snacks, soda, fast food) than for complex or high-stakes purchases.
segments.tr: - Il fonctionne généralement mieux pour les **produits familiers, à faible risque et à faible implication** (encas, sodas, restauration rapide) que pour les achats complexes ou à fort enjeu.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dans la vie quotidienne

segments.src: Jordan, who lives in Columbus, Ohio, is watching football on Sunday.
segments.tr: Jordan, qui vit à Columbus, dans l'Ohio, regarde un match de football le dimanche.

segments.src: During a commercial break, a goofy car insurance ad gets a laugh.
segments.tr: Pendant une pause publicitaire, une publicité d'assurance automobile loufoque fait rire.

segments.src: Jordan isn't shopping for insurance right now, so the joke and the memorable mascot are basically all that sticks.
segments.tr: Jordan n'est pas en train de chercher une assurance pour le moment, donc seuls la blague et la mascotte mémorable restent vraiment.

segments.src: That's the **peripheral route**, and it worked: the brand name is now in Jordan's head.
segments.tr: C'est la **voie périphérique**, et elle a fonctionné : le nom de la marque est désormais dans la tête de Jordan.

segments.src: Three weeks later, Jordan's policy is up for renewal, and the quotes are around $1,400 a year.
segments.tr: Trois semaines plus tard, le contrat d'assurance de Jordan arrive à renouvellement, et les devis tournent autour de 1 400 $ par an.

segments.src: Now Jordan is motivated and sits down with a laptop to compare deductibles, liability limits, and customer reviews.
segments.tr: Jordan est maintenant motivé et s'installe devant un ordinateur portable pour comparer les franchises, les plafonds de responsabilité civile et les avis des clients.

segments.src: That's the **central route**.
segments.tr: C'est la **voie centrale**.

segments.src: A funny ad won't close this sale.
segments.tr: Une publicité drôle ne conclura pas cette vente.

segments.src: Clear numbers and believable claims will.
segments.tr: Des chiffres clairs et des affirmations crédibles, si.

segments.src: Later that week, Jordan sees a public service ad from the CDC's long-running "Tips From Former Smokers" campaign, which features real people living with smoking-related illnesses.
segments.tr: Plus tard dans la semaine, Jordan voit une annonce d'intérêt public de la campagne de longue date des CDC, « Tips From Former Smokers », qui met en scène de vraies personnes atteintes de maladies liées au tabac.

segments.src: The ad is frightening, but it ends with a concrete step: call 1-800-QUIT-NOW for free help.
segments.tr: La publicité est effrayante, mais elle se termine par une action concrète : appeler le 1-800-QUIT-NOW pour obtenir une aide gratuite.

segments.src: It pairs **threat with efficacy**, which is how a fear appeal is supposed to be built.
segments.tr: Elle associe **menace et efficacité**, ce qui est la façon dont un appel à la peur est censé être construit.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Résumé en 3 lignes

pt.title: [Psicologia do Consumidor #6] Por que um anúncio engraçado pode vender batata frita, mas não um carro: como a persuasão realmente funciona

segments.src: > An ad persuades in different ways depending on how much you care and how closely you're paying attention. Fear and humor can both work, but only when they're used carefully.
segments.tr: > Um anúncio persuade de formas diferentes dependendo de quanto você se importa e de quão atentamente presta atenção. Medo e humor podem funcionar, mas só quando são usados com cuidado.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de Hoje

segments.src: Every ad is trying to change something in your head, whether that's a belief ("this brand is reliable"), a feeling ("this brand is fun"), or a behavior ("buy now").
segments.tr: Todo anúncio tenta mudar algo na sua cabeça, seja uma crença (“esta marca é confiável”), um sentimento (“esta marca é divertida”) ou um comportamento (“compre agora”).

segments.src: Persuasion is the process of making that change.
segments.tr: Persuasão é o processo de realizar essa mudança.

segments.src: Researchers have spent decades studying **why some messages work and others don't.**
segments.tr: Pesquisadores passaram décadas estudando **por que algumas mensagens funcionam e outras não.**

segments.src: The Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM)**
segments.tr: O Modelo de Probabilidade de Elaboração (ELM)**

segments.src: Psychologists Richard Petty and John Cacioppo proposed the ELM in the 1980s.
segments.tr: Os psicólogos Richard Petty e John Cacioppo propuseram o ELM nos anos 1980.

segments.src: Its main idea is that people process a persuasive message along one of two routes:
segments.tr: Sua ideia principal é que as pessoas processam uma mensagem persuasiva por uma de duas rotas:

segments.src: - **Central route.** You think carefully about the message: Is the evidence good? Do the claims hold up? People take this route when they are **motivated** (the decision matters to them) and **able** (they have the time, attention, and knowledge). Attitudes formed this way tend to last longer and are harder to change.
segments.tr: - **Rota central.** Você pensa cuidadosamente na mensagem: a evidência é boa? As afirmações se sustentam? As pessoas seguem essa rota quando estão **motivadas** (a decisão importa para elas) e **capazes** (têm tempo, atenção e conhecimento). Atitudes formadas dessa forma tendem a durar mais e são mais difíceis de mudar.

segments.src: - **Peripheral route.** You rely on shortcuts such as an attractive spokesperson, a catchy jingle, a celebrity, or simply "lots of people bought it." People take this route when they're distracted, in a hurry, or don't care much. Attitudes formed this way can shift quickly, and they can fade just as quickly.
segments.tr: - **Rota periférica.** Você recorre a atalhos, como um porta-voz atraente, um jingle chiclete, uma celebridade ou simplesmente “muita gente comprou”. As pessoas seguem essa rota quando estão distraídas, com pressa ou não se importam muito. Atitudes formadas dessa forma podem mudar rapidamente e também podem desaparecer com a mesma rapidez.

segments.src: "Elaboration" just means how much you think about the message.
segments.tr: “Elaboração” significa apenas o quanto você pensa sobre a mensagem.

segments.src: The same ad can persuade one person through careful reasoning and another through a smiling face.
segments.tr: O mesmo anúncio pode persuadir uma pessoa por meio de raciocínio cuidadoso e outra por meio de um rosto sorridente.

segments.src: Fear appeals**
segments.tr: Apelos ao medo**

segments.src: A fear appeal shows a threat, such as illness, an accident, or financial loss, to motivate action.
segments.tr: Um apelo ao medo mostra uma ameaça, como doença, acidente ou prejuízo financeiro, para motivar uma ação.

segments.src: Research, including Kim Witte's Extended Parallel Process Model, suggests that fear works only when it comes with **efficacy**: the audience has to believe there's a clear, doable step that will actually protect them.
segments.tr: Pesquisas, incluindo o Extended Parallel Process Model, de Kim Witte, sugerem que o medo só funciona quando vem acompanhado de **eficácia**: o público precisa acreditar que existe um passo claro e viável que de fato o protegerá.

segments.src: When a message has high threat and low efficacy, people often push it away instead of acting on it.
segments.tr: Quando uma mensagem tem alta ameaça e baixa eficácia, as pessoas costumam rejeitá-la em vez de agir.

segments.src: They avoid the topic, doubt the source, or tell themselves "it won't happen to me."
segments.tr: Elas evitam o assunto, desconfiam da fonte ou se convencem de que “isso não vai acontecer comigo”.

segments.src: Scaring people harder doesn't automatically make the message work better.
segments.tr: Assustar mais as pessoas não torna a mensagem automaticamente mais eficaz.

segments.src: Humor appeals**
segments.tr: Apelos ao humor**

segments.src: Humor grabs attention and makes people like the ad, and that good feeling can rub off on the brand.
segments.tr: O humor chama a atenção e faz as pessoas gostarem do anúncio, e essa boa sensação pode se transferir para a marca.

segments.src: It has downsides, though:
segments.tr: Mas ele tem desvantagens:

segments.src: - It can **distract** viewers from the actual product information.
segments.tr: - Pode **distrair** o espectador da informação real sobre o produto.

segments.src: - People may remember the joke and forget the brand, which practitioners sometimes call the "vampire effect."
segments.tr: - As pessoas podem lembrar da piada e esquecer a marca, efeito que profissionais às vezes chamam de “efeito vampiro”.

segments.src: - It usually works better for **familiar, low-risk, low-involvement products** (snacks, soda, fast food) than for complex or high-stakes purchases.
segments.tr: - Costuma funcionar melhor para **produtos familiares, de baixo risco e baixo envolvimento** (lanches, refrigerantes, fast food) do que para compras complexas ou de alto risco.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## No Dia a Dia

segments.src: Jordan, who lives in Columbus, Ohio, is watching football on Sunday.
segments.tr: Jordan, que mora em Columbus, Ohio, está assistindo a futebol americano no domingo.

segments.src: During a commercial break, a goofy car insurance ad gets a laugh.
segments.tr: Durante o intervalo, um anúncio bobo de seguro de carro arranca risadas.

segments.src: Jordan isn't shopping for insurance right now, so the joke and the memorable mascot are basically all that sticks.
segments.tr: Jordan não está procurando seguro agora, então a piada e a mascote memorável são basicamente tudo o que fica.

segments.src: That's the **peripheral route**, and it worked: the brand name is now in Jordan's head.
segments.tr: Isso é a **rota periférica**, e funcionou: o nome da marca agora está na cabeça de Jordan.

segments.src: Three weeks later, Jordan's policy is up for renewal, and the quotes are around $1,400 a year.
segments.tr: Três semanas depois, a apólice de Jordan está perto de ser renovada, e as cotações giram em torno de US$ 1.400 por ano.

segments.src: Now Jordan is motivated and sits down with a laptop to compare deductibles, liability limits, and customer reviews.
segments.tr: Agora Jordan está motivado e senta-se com um notebook para comparar franquias, limites de responsabilidade civil e avaliações de clientes.

segments.src: That's the **central route**.
segments.tr: Essa é a **rota central**.

segments.src: A funny ad won't close this sale.
segments.tr: Um anúncio engraçado não fecha essa venda.

segments.src: Clear numbers and believable claims will.
segments.tr: Números claros e afirmações críveis, sim.

segments.src: Later that week, Jordan sees a public service ad from the CDC's long-running "Tips From Former Smokers" campaign, which features real people living with smoking-related illnesses.
segments.tr: No fim da semana, Jordan vê um anúncio de utilidade pública da campanha de longa data dos CDC “Tips From Former Smokers”, que apresenta pessoas reais convivendo com doenças relacionadas ao tabagismo.

segments.src: The ad is frightening, but it ends with a concrete step: call 1-800-QUIT-NOW for free help.
segments.tr: O anúncio é assustador, mas termina com um passo concreto: ligar para 1-800-QUIT-NOW para receber ajuda gratuita.

segments.src: It pairs **threat with efficacy**, which is how a fear appeal is supposed to be built.
segments.tr: Ele combina **ameaça com eficácia**, que é como um apelo ao medo deve ser construído.

segments.tr: ## Resumo em 3 Linhas

segments.tr: 1. Segundo o ELM, as pessoas processam anúncios por uma **rota central** cuidadosa ou por uma **rota periférica** baseada em atalhos, dependendo de sua motivação e capacidade.

segments.tr: 3. O **humor** aumenta a atenção e a simpatia, mas pode ofuscar a mensagem. Ele se adapta melhor a produtos de baixo envolvimento do que a produtos de alto risco.

ja.title: [消費者心理学 #6] おもしろい広告はポテトチップスは売れても車は売れない理由：説得は実際にどう働くのか

segments.src: > An ad persuades in different ways depending on how much you care and how closely you're paying attention. Fear and humor can both work, but only when they're used carefully.
segments.tr: > 広告は、あなたがどれだけ気にかけ、どれだけ注意深く見ているかによって、異なる仕方で説得します。恐怖もユーモアも効果を持ちえますが、慎重に使われた場合に限られます。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日のコンセプト

segments.src: Every ad is trying to change something in your head, whether that's a belief ("this brand is reliable"), a feeling ("this brand is fun"), or a behavior ("buy now").
segments.tr: どの広告も、あなたの頭の中の何かを変えようとしています。それは信念（「このブランドは信頼できる」）、感情（「このブランドは楽しい」）、行動（「今すぐ買おう」）のいずれかです。

segments.src: Persuasion is the process of making that change.
segments.tr: 説得とは、その変化を生み出すプロセスのことです。

segments.src: Researchers have spent decades studying **why some messages work and others don't.**
segments.tr: 研究者たちは数十年にわたり、**なぜある伝え方はうまくいき、別の伝え方はうまくいかないのか**を研究してきました。

segments.src: The Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM)**
segments.tr: 精緻化見込みモデル（ELM）**

segments.src: Psychologists Richard Petty and John Cacioppo proposed the ELM in the 1980s.
segments.tr: 心理学者のリチャード・ペティとジョン・カシオッポは、1980年代にELMを提唱しました。

segments.src: Its main idea is that people process a persuasive message along one of two routes:
segments.tr: その主要な考え方は、人は説得的なメッセージを次の2つのルートのいずれかで処理する、というものです：

segments.src: - **Central route.** You think carefully about the message: Is the evidence good? Do the claims hold up? People take this route when they are **motivated** (the decision matters to them) and **able** (they have the time, attention, and knowledge). Attitudes formed this way tend to last longer and are harder to change.
segments.tr: - **中心的ルート。** メッセージについて注意深く考えます。証拠は良いか？主張は成り立つか？人は、その決定が自分にとって重要であり（**動機**がある）、時間・注意力・知識もある（**能力**がある）とき、このルートをたどります。この経路で形成された態度は長続きし、変えにくい傾向があります。

segments.src: - **Peripheral route.** You rely on shortcuts such as an attractive spokesperson, a catchy jingle, a celebrity, or simply "lots of people bought it." People take this route when they're distracted, in a hurry, or don't care much. Attitudes formed this way can shift quickly, and they can fade just as quickly.
segments.tr: - **周辺的ルート。** 魅力的な広告モデル、耳に残るジングル、有名人、あるいは単に「多くの人が買っている」といった手がかりに頼ります。気が散っているとき、急いでいるとき、あまり関心がないときに、人はこのルートをたどります。この経路で形成された態度は素早く変わることがありますが、同じくらい素早く薄れることもあります。

segments.src: "Elaboration" just means how much you think about the message.
segments.tr: 「精緻化（elaboration）」とは、メッセージについてどれだけ考えるか、という意味にすぎません。

segments.src: The same ad can persuade one person through careful reasoning and another through a smiling face.
segments.tr: 同じ広告でも、ある人は慎重な推論によって説得され、別の人は笑顔の人物によって説得されることがあります。

segments.src: Fear appeals**
segments.tr: 恐怖訴求**

segments.src: A fear appeal shows a threat, such as illness, an accident, or financial loss, to motivate action.
segments.tr: 恐怖訴求とは、病気・事故・経済的損失などの脅威を示して、行動を促す手法です。

segments.src: Research, including Kim Witte's Extended Parallel Process Model, suggests that fear works only when it comes with **efficacy**: the audience has to believe there's a clear, doable step that will actually protect them.
segments.tr: Kim Witteの拡張並行過程モデル（EPPM）を含む研究によれば、恐怖は**効力感**を伴う場合にのみ機能します。効力感とは、自分を実際に守ってくれる明確で実行可能な手段がある、と受け手が信じられる状態のことです。

segments.src: When a message has high threat and low efficacy, people often push it away instead of acting on it.
segments.tr: 脅威が大きく効力感が低いメッセージでは、人は行動するのではなく、それを遠ざけてしまうことが多くなります。

segments.src: They avoid the topic, doubt the source, or tell themselves "it won't happen to me."
segments.tr: 話題を避けたり、情報源を疑ったり、「自分には起こらない」と思い込んだりします。

segments.src: Scaring people harder doesn't automatically make the message work better.
segments.tr: 人をより強く怖がらせれば、メッセージの効果が自動的に高まるわけではありません。

segments.src: Humor appeals**
segments.tr: ユーモア訴求**

segments.src: Humor grabs attention and makes people like the ad, and that good feeling can rub off on the brand.
segments.tr: ユーモアは注意を引き、人に広告を好きにさせます。そしてその好感がブランドにも移ることがあります。

segments.src: It has downsides, though:
segments.tr: ただし欠点もあります：

segments.src: - It can **distract** viewers from the actual product information.
segments.tr: - 視聴者の注意が、実際の製品情報から**それてしまう**ことがあります。

segments.src: - People may remember the joke and forget the brand, which practitioners sometimes call the "vampire effect."
segments.tr: - 人はジョークは覚えていても、ブランドを忘れることがあります。実務家はこれを「吸血鬼効果（vampire effect）」と呼ぶことがあります。

segments.src: - It usually works better for **familiar, low-risk, low-involvement products** (snacks, soda, fast food) than for complex or high-stakes purchases.
segments.tr: - 一般に、複雑な購入や重大な購入よりも、身近で低リスク・低関与の商品（スナック、ソーダ、ファストフードなど）に向いています。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活では

segments.src: Jordan, who lives in Columbus, Ohio, is watching football on Sunday.
segments.tr: オハイオ州コロンバスに住むJordanは、日曜日にフットボールを観ています。

segments.src: That's the **peripheral route**, and it worked: the brand name is now in Jordan's head.
segments.tr: これは**周辺的ルート**であり、効果がありました。ブランド名がJordanの頭に入ったのです。

segments.src: Three weeks later, Jordan's policy is up for renewal, and the quotes are around $1,400 a year.
segments.tr: 3週間後、Jordanの保険契約の更新時期が来て、見積もりは年間約1,400ドルです。

segments.src: Now Jordan is motivated and sits down with a laptop to compare deductibles, liability limits, and customer reviews.
segments.tr: 今やJordanは動機を持ち、ノートパソコンの前に座って、免責額・賠償責任の上限・顧客レビューを比較します。

segments.src: That's the **central route**.

segments.src: A funny ad won't close this sale.

segments.src: Clear numbers and believable claims will.

segments.src: Later that week, Jordan sees a public service ad from the CDC's long-running "Tips From Former Smokers" campaign, which features real people living with smoking-related illnesses.

segments.src: The ad is frightening, but it ends with a concrete step: call 1-800-QUIT-NOW for free help.
segments.tr: その広告は恐ろしいものですが、最後に具体的な行動が示されます。無料の支援を受けるために1-800-QUIT-NOWに電話してください、と。

segments.tr: これは**脅威と効力感を組み合わせる**もので、恐怖訴求が本来そう作られるべきという形になっています。

segments.tr: ## 3行まとめ

segments.tr: Die Psychologen Richard Petty und John Cacioppo stellten das ELM in den 1980er-Jahren vor.

segments.src: Its main idea is that people process a persuasive message along one of two routes:
segments.tr: Die Kernidee lautet, dass Menschen eine überzeugende Botschaft auf einem von zwei Wegen verarbeiten:

segments.src: - **Central route.** You think carefully about the message: Is the evidence good? Do the claims hold up? People take this route when they are **motivated** (the decision matters to them) and **able** (they have the time, attention, and knowledge). Attitudes formed this way tend to last longer and are harder to change.
segments.tr: - **Zentrale Route.** Sie denken genau über die Botschaft nach: Ist die Beweislage gut? Halten die Behauptungen einer Prüfung stand? Menschen nehmen diesen Weg, wenn sie **motiviert** sind (die Entscheidung ist ihnen wichtig) und **fähig** (sie haben Zeit, Aufmerksamkeit und Wissen). Auf diesem Weg gebildete Einstellungen halten tendenziell länger und sind schwerer zu ändern.

segments.src: - **Peripheral route.** You rely on shortcuts such as an attractive spokesperson, a catchy jingle, a celebrity, or simply "lots of people bought it." People take this route when they're distracted, in a hurry, or don't care much. Attitudes formed this way can shift quickly, and they can fade just as quickly.
segments.tr: - **Periphere Route.** Sie verlassen sich auf Abkürzungen wie eine attraktive Werbefigur, einen eingängigen Jingle, eine Berühmtheit oder einfach „das kaufen viele“. Menschen nehmen diesen Weg, wenn sie abgelenkt sind, es eilig haben oder sich wenig dafür interessieren. Auf diesem Weg gebildete Einstellungen können sich schnell verschieben und verblassen ebenso schnell.

segments.src: "Elaboration" just means how much you think about the message.
segments.tr: „Elaboration“ bedeutet einfach, wie intensiv Sie über die Botschaft nachdenken.

segments.src: The same ad can persuade one person through careful reasoning and another through a smiling face.
segments.tr: Dieselbe Werbung kann die eine Person durch sorgfältiges Abwägen überzeugen und eine andere durch ein lächelndes Gesicht.

segments.src: Fear appeals**
segments.tr: Angstappelle**

segments.src: A fear appeal shows a threat, such as illness, an accident, or financial loss, to motivate action.
segments.tr: Ein Angstappell zeigt eine Bedrohung, etwa Krankheit, einen Unfall oder finanzielle Verluste, um zum Handeln zu bewegen.

segments.src: Research, including Kim Witte's Extended Parallel Process Model, suggests that fear works only when it comes with **efficacy**: the audience has to believe there's a clear, doable step that will actually protect them.
segments.tr: Untersuchungen, darunter Kim Wittes Extended Parallel Process Model, legen nahe, dass Angst nur dann wirkt, wenn sie mit **Wirksamkeit** (Efficacy) einhergeht: Das Publikum muss glauben, dass es einen klaren, machbaren Schritt gibt, der es tatsächlich schützt.

segments.src: When a message has high threat and low efficacy, people often push it away instead of acting on it.
segments.tr: Wenn eine Botschaft hohe Bedrohung mit geringer Wirksamkeit verbindet, weisen Menschen sie oft zurück, statt danach zu handeln.

segments.src: They avoid the topic, doubt the source, or tell themselves "it won't happen to me."
segments.tr: Sie meiden das Thema, bezweifeln die Quelle oder sagen sich: „Das passiert mir nicht.“

segments.src: Scaring people harder doesn't automatically make the message work better.
segments.tr: Menschen stärker zu erschrecken macht eine Botschaft nicht automatisch wirksamer.

segments.src: Humor appeals**
segments.tr: Humorappelle**

segments.src: Humor grabs attention and makes people like the ad, and that good feeling can rub off on the brand.
segments.tr: Humor erregt Aufmerksamkeit und sorgt dafür, dass Menschen die Werbung mögen; dieses gute Gefühl kann auf die Marke abfärben.

segments.src: It has downsides, though:
segments.tr: Er hat aber auch Nachteile:

segments.src: - It can **distract** viewers from the actual product information.
segments.tr: - Er kann Zuschauer **von der eigentlichen Produktinformation ablenken**.

segments.src: - People may remember the joke and forget the brand, which practitioners sometimes call the "vampire effect."
segments.tr: - Menschen erinnern sich womöglich an den Witz und vergessen die Marke, was Praktiker manchmal als „Vampireffekt“ bezeichnen.

segments.src: - It usually works better for **familiar, low-risk, low-involvement products** (snacks, soda, fast food) than for complex or high-stakes purchases.
segments.tr: - Er funktioniert meist besser bei **vertrauten, risikoarmen Produkten mit geringem Engagement** (Snacks, Limonade, Fast Food) als bei komplexen oder folgenreichen Käufen.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: Jordan, who lives in Columbus, Ohio, is watching football on Sunday.
segments.tr: Jordan, die in Columbus, Ohio, lebt, schaut am Sonntag Football.

segments.src: During a commercial break, a goofy car insurance ad gets a laugh.
segments.tr: In einer Werbepause sorgt eine alberne Autoversicherungswerbung für Gelächter.

segments.src: Jordan isn't shopping for insurance right now, so the joke and the memorable mascot are basically all that sticks.
segments.tr: Jordan sucht gerade keine Versicherung, deshalb bleiben im Grunde nur der Witz und das einprägsame Maskottchen hängen.

segments.src: That's the **peripheral route**, and it worked: the brand name is now in Jordan's head.
segments.tr: Das ist die **periphere Route**, und sie hat funktioniert: Der Markenname ist jetzt in Jordans Kopf.

segments.src: Three weeks later, Jordan's policy is up for renewal, and the quotes are around $1,400 a year.
segments.tr: Drei Wochen später steht Jordans Police zur Verlängerung an, und die Angebote liegen bei etwa 1.400 Dollar pro Jahr.

segments.src: Now Jordan is motivated and sits down with a laptop to compare deductibles, liability limits, and customer reviews.
segments.tr: Jetzt ist Jordan motiviert und setzt sich mit einem Laptop hin, um Selbstbeteiligungen, Haftungsgrenzen und Kundenbewertungen zu vergleichen.

segments.src: That's the **central route**.
segments.tr: Das ist die **zentrale Route**.

segments.src: A funny ad won't close this sale.
segments.tr: Eine witzige Werbung schließt diesen Verkauf nicht ab.

segments.src: Clear numbers and believable claims will.
segments.tr: Klare Zahlen und glaubwürdige Behauptungen tun es.

segments.src: Later that week, Jordan sees a public service ad from the CDC's long-running "Tips From Former Smokers" campaign, which features real people living with smoking-related illnesses.
segments.tr: Später in dieser Woche sieht Jordan eine Public-Service-Anzeige der CDC aus der seit Langem laufenden Kampagne „Tips From Former Smokers“, die echte Menschen mit rauchbedingten Krankheiten zeigt.

segments.src: The ad is frightening, but it ends with a concrete step: call 1-800-QUIT-NOW for free help.
segments.tr: Die Anzeige ist erschreckend, endet aber mit einem konkreten Schritt: die kostenlose Hilfe unter 1-800-QUIT-NOW anrufen.

segments.src: It pairs **threat with efficacy**, which is how a fear appeal is supposed to be built.
segments.tr: Sie verbindet **Bedrohung mit Wirksamkeit**, so wie ein Angstappell aufgebaut sein sollte.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Zusammenfassung in drei Zeilen

segments.src: 1. According to the ELM, people process ads through a careful **central route** or a shortcut-based **peripheral route**, depending on their motivation and ability.
segments.tr: 1. Laut ELM verarbeiten Menschen Werbung je nach Motivation und Fähigkeit entweder über die sorgfältige **zentrale Route** oder über die abkürzende **periphere Route**.

segments.src: 2. **Fear appeals** work best when the threat comes with a clear, doable solution. Fear without a way out tends to cause avoidance.
segments.tr: 2. **Angstappelle** wirken am besten, wenn die Bedrohung mit einer klaren, machbaren Lösung einhergeht. Angst ohne Ausweg führt eher zur Vermeidung.

segments.src: 3. **Humor** boosts attention and liking but can bury the message. It fits low-involvement products better than high-stakes ones.
segments.tr: 3. **Humor** steigert Aufmerksamkeit und Sympathie, kann die Botschaft aber verdecken. Er passt besser zu Produkten mit geringem Engagement als zu folgenreichen.
